question: Among the following routes of drug administration, the most rapid onset of action occurs with the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. intravenous route

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The intravenous route puts the whole dose directly into the blood stream, so the effect begins almost at once and the drug is fully available

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — topical route: A drug applied to the skin acts only locally and enters the circulation slowly

B — subcutaneous route: Absorption from the subcutaneous tissue takes several minutes

C — oral route: An oral drug must dissolve, be absorbed and pass through the liver before it acts

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Because the intravenous effect is immediate, the dose is given slowly and the patient is watched continuously, since an error cannot be recalled

question: Bioavailability of a drug means the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. fraction of the administered dose that reaches the blood stream in an active form

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Bioavailability describes how much of the dose actually reaches the systemic circulation unchanged and is therefore able to act

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — total amount of the drug in the bottle: The quantity in the container is the stock, not the availability

C — time taken for the drug to be excreted: The time taken for excretion describes elimination

D — strength printed on the label: The label strength is the concentration of the preparation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The bioavailability of the same drug differs between the oral and the intravenous route, which is why the oral dose is usually larger
option_1: total amount of the drug in the bottle
option_2: fraction of the administered dose that reaches the blood stream in an active form
option_3: time taken for the drug to be excreted

question: One gram of a drug is equal to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1000 milligrams

🧠 Clinical Rationale: One gram contains one thousand milligrams, so a prescription written in grams must be converted before the dose is drawn up

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 100 milligrams: One hundred milligrams is one tenth of a gram

C — 10 milligrams: Ten milligrams is one hundredth of a gram

D — 10,000 milligrams: Ten thousand milligrams is ten grams

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The units on the prescription and on the label are read together every time, since the commonest serious drug error is a decimal shift between grams and milligrams

question: An intravenous infusion of 1000 millilitres is to be given over 8 hours through a set that delivers 15 drops to a millilitre. The drip rate per minute is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 31 drops

🧠 Clinical Rationale: One thousand multiplied by fifteen gives fifteen thousand drops, and dividing by four hundred and eighty minutes gives about thirty one drops a minute

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 45 drops: Forty five drops a minute would finish it in under six hours

C — 21 drops: Twenty one drops a minute would run the bottle in about twelve hours

D — 62 drops: Sixty two drops a minute is about double the correct rate

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The rate is counted with a watch at the start and rechecked each hour, since the flow changes when the arm is moved or the cannula shifts

question: A child weighing 20 kilograms is prescribed 15 milligrams per kilogram per day of a drug in three divided doses. Each dose is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 100 milligrams

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The total daily dose is twenty multiplied by fifteen, which is three hundred milligrams, and one third of it, that is one hundred milligrams, is given at a time

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 300 milligrams: Three hundred milligrams is the whole day's dose

C — 50 milligrams: Fifty milligrams is half of the correct single dose

D — 150 milligrams: One hundred and fifty milligrams is half of the daily dose

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Paediatric doses calculated from the weight are always cross-checked with a second nurse before they are given

question: Oral medication is withheld in a patient who is vomiting because:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. the drug will not be absorbed and may be lost with the vomit

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A drug that is vomited out is neither absorbed nor counted, so the patient receives an unpredictable dose and the treatment fails

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the drug will act too quickly: Vomiting slows absorption and does not hasten the effect

B — the drug will damage the stomach: The stomach is not damaged by the usual drugs in this situation

D — the drug will be absorbed in the lungs: Drugs are not absorbed from the lungs when given by mouth

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The prescribed alternative route, such as the intravenous route, is used until the patient can retain oral fluids, and the vomiting is investigated
option_3: the drug will not be absorbed and may be lost with the vomit
option_4: the drug will be absorbed in the lungs

question: The antibiotic for which a test dose is given before the first full dose, because of the risk of a severe reaction, is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. penicillin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Penicillin can cause anaphylaxis, so the history of allergy is taken and the drug is given only where emergency drugs and equipment are at hand

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — ranitidine: Ranitidine is an antacid and is not given as a test dose

C — paracetamol: Paracetamol is an analgesic and does not require a test dose

D — metronidazole: Metronidazole is well tolerated and is not given in this way

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Adrenaline must be available whenever a penicillin injection is given, since a severe reaction begins within minutes and cannot be treated later

question: Tetracycline is avoided in children below eight years of age because it:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. is deposited in the growing teeth and bones, staining the teeth permanently

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The drug binds to calcium in the growing teeth and bones, which produces permanent yellow brown staining of the teeth and can affect bone growth

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — causes kidney failure: Kidney damage is associated with the aminoglycosides and some other drugs

B — causes deafness: Deafness is a risk with the aminoglycosides and not with tetracycline

C — has no effect on the infection: Tetracycline is an effective antibiotic in the infections for which it is used

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The same rule applies in pregnancy, since the drug crosses the placenta and affects the teeth of the unborn baby
option_4: is deposited in the growing teeth and bones, staining the teeth permanently

question: The most important consequence of the widespread and unnecessary use of antibiotics is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the development of organisms resistant to antibiotics

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Every unnecessary dose selects the organisms that can survive, and these resistant strains then spread in the hospital and in the community

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — an increase in the body weight: Body weight is not affected in this way

C — a fall in the cost of treatment: Resistance in fact raises the cost, since newer and more expensive drugs have to be used

D — a rise in the white cell count: The white cell count is not raised by the drug itself

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse's contribution to this problem is to give the antibiotic at the correct time, in the correct dose and for the full prescribed course
option_2: the development of organisms resistant to antibiotics
option_3: a fall in the cost of treatment
option_4: a rise in the white cell count

question: Gentamicin is given cautiously and the dose adjusted because it may damage the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. kidney and the eighth cranial nerve

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The aminoglycosides are excreted by the kidney and are toxic to the renal tubule as well as to the cochlear and vestibular parts of the eighth nerve

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — lungs: The lungs are not the target of this toxicity

C — skin: A skin rash may occur but is not the reason for caution

D — liver only: These drugs are well known for kidney damage and not for liver damage

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The blood level, the kidney function and any giddiness, ringing in the ear or loss of hearing are checked daily during the course

question: The laboratory test used to monitor a patient who is taking warfarin is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. prothrombin time, reported as the international normalised ratio

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Warfarin blocks the vitamin K dependent clotting factors, and the prothrombin time with the international normalised ratio shows how far the clotting has been prolonged

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — platelet count: The platelet count is not affected by warfarin

C — bleeding time: The bleeding time tests the platelets and the small vessels

D — erythrocyte sedimentation rate: The sedimentation rate is a general test of inflammation

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The blood sample is taken at the same time each day, since the result decides the dose given that evening
option_2: prothrombin time, reported as the international normalised ratio

question: The drug given to reverse the effect of an overdose of warfarin is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. vitamin K

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Vitamin K restores the synthesis of the clotting factors that warfarin has blocked, and fresh frozen plasma is given if the bleeding is severe

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — adrenaline: Adrenaline is used in anaphylaxis and cardiac arrest

C — atropine: Atropine is used for a slow pulse and in organophosphate poisoning

D — protamine sulphate: Protamine sulphate reverses heparin and has no effect on warfarin

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Vitamin K takes several hours to act, so a patient with active bleeding is not managed by vitamin K alone

question: A 60-year-old man who has been taking warfarin for three months asks what he should be careful about. The nurse should advise him to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. take the drug at the same time every day, keep the diet steady, avoid taking other medicines without advice and report any bleeding at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A steady intake, regular timing and prompt reporting of bleeding keep the treatment safe, and any new medicine is checked for interaction

🔍 Key Clues: 60-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — double the dose on the days when he eats more vegetables: Changing the dose without a blood test can cause serious bleeding

C — take the drug only when the blood report is abnormal: The drug is taken daily, and the report is used to adjust the dose and not to decide whether to take it

D — stop the drug when he feels well: Stopping on his own allows a clot to form

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is asked to report black stools, blood in the urine, bleeding gums and unusual bruising, which are the earliest signs of over-treatment
option_1: take the drug at the same time every day, keep the diet steady, avoid taking other medicines without advice and report any bleeding at once
option_2: double the dose on the days when he eats more vegetables
option_3: take the drug only when the blood report is abnormal
option_4: stop the drug when he feels well

question: A drug is available as 250 milligrams in 5 millilitres. The volume to be drawn up for a prescribed dose of 400 milligrams is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 8 millilitres

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Each millilitre contains fifty milligrams, so four hundred milligrams needs eight millilitres

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 5 millilitres: Five millilitres gives only two hundred and fifty milligrams

B — 10 millilitres: Ten millilitres gives five hundred milligrams, which is a dangerous overdose

C — 6 millilitres: Six millilitres gives three hundred milligrams

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The calculation is done from the label strength and checked with a second nurse before the drug is drawn up

question: Because of the first pass effect through the liver:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the oral dose of a drug is usually larger than the parenteral dose

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Part of an absorbed oral dose is metabolised in the liver before it reaches the general circulation, so a larger dose is needed to produce the same blood level

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the oral route acts faster than the intravenous route: The intravenous route always acts faster than the oral route

C — all drugs are given by injection: Most drugs are still given by mouth, as it is the safest and most convenient route

D — the liver destroys all the drug given by mouth: Only a part and not all of the drug is metabolised at this stage

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: Drugs given under the tongue or by the rectal route escape this first pass metabolism, which is why some of them are prescribed by those routes
option_1: the oral route acts faster than the intravenous route
option_2: the oral dose of a drug is usually larger than the parenteral dose
option_4: the liver destroys all the drug given by mouth

question: A 70-year-old man who has received broad spectrum antibiotics for a week develops profuse watery diarrhoea with a foul smell and a raised temperature. The most likely cause is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. overgrowth of Clostridium difficile in the bowel

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The normal bowel flora are destroyed by the antibiotic, which allows Clostridium difficile to multiply and produce a toxin that causes this diarrhoea

🔍 Key Clues: 70-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — lactose intolerance: Lactose intolerance gives wind and loose stools rather than this acute picture with fever

B — a urinary tract infection: A urinary infection does not produce diarrhoea of this kind

C — food poisoning from the hospital diet: Food poisoning usually affects several patients at the same time

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is placed on contact precautions, the stool is sent for the toxin test, and the antibiotics are reviewed, since a severe attack can cause a dangerous dilatation of the bowel
option_4: overgrowth of Clostridium difficile in the bowel

question: Which anticoagulant is given subcutaneously and does not need routine laboratory monitoring of its effect?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. low molecular weight heparin

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Low molecular weight heparin has a predictable effect, so it is given in a fixed dose by the subcutaneous route without daily blood tests

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — aspirin: Aspirin is an antiplatelet drug and its effect is not monitored in this way

B — heparin given intravenously: Intravenous heparin needs the activated partial thromboplastin time to be checked frequently

C — warfarin: Warfarin needs the prothrombin time with the international normalised ratio at regular intervals

⚠️ Exam Trap: Check the dose, route and timing before choosing - the right drug in the wrong dose is a wrong answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The dose depends on the body weight and the kidney function, and the platelet count is watched because this drug can rarely cause a fall in platelets

question: The temperature and pressure used in an autoclave for sterilisation are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 121 degrees Celsius at 15 pounds per square inch for 15 to 20 minutes

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Steam under pressure at one hundred and twenty one degrees Celsius and fifteen pounds per square inch kills even the bacterial spores within fifteen to twenty minutes

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 60 degrees Celsius for one hour: Sixty degrees is used for pasteurisation and not for sterilisation

B — 100 degrees Celsius at normal pressure for 10 minutes: Boiling at one hundred degrees kills most bacteria but not the spores

C — 180 degrees Celsius for 5 minutes: One hundred and eighty degrees is used in a hot air oven and not in an autoclave

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The articles are placed loosely so that the steam reaches every surface, and the date of sterilisation is written on every pack
option_2: 100 degrees Celsius at normal pressure for 10 minutes
option_4: 121 degrees Celsius at 15 pounds per square inch for 15 to 20 minutes

question: The commonest medium used in the laboratory to grow bacteria from a clinical specimen is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. nutrient agar

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Nutrient agar gives the moisture, the nutrients and the solid surface on which bacteria multiply and form colonies that can be identified

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — distilled water: Distilled water has no nutrients and is in fact harmful to the organisms

B — normal saline: Normal saline keeps the specimen moist during transport but does not support growth

D — glucose solution: A glucose solution alone cannot support the growth of most bacteria

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The specimen is collected before the first dose of the antibiotic, because the drug already in the body may prevent the organism from growing in the laboratory

question: A pus sample from a patient with a wound infection is sent for culture and sensitivity. The purpose of this test is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. identify the organism and find the antibiotic to which it is sensitive

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Culture grows the organism and the sensitivity test shows which antibiotics will kill it, so that treatment is targeted and not merely guessed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — count the number of white cells in the pus: The cell count is not the purpose of the test

B — decide whether a dressing is needed: The need for a dressing is a nursing decision made from the condition of the wound

C — measure the extent of the wound: The size of the wound is assessed by inspection

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The report is read with the clinical picture, since an organism grown from the surface may be a contaminant rather than the true cause of the infection
option_1: count the number of white cells in the pus
option_4: identify the organism and find the antibiotic to which it is sensitive

question: The medium used for the culture of Mycobacterium tuberculosis is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Lowenstein-Jensen medium

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The tubercle bacillus grows slowly and needs an enriched egg based medium, and the growth takes several weeks

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — blood agar: Blood agar grows most pyogenic organisms

B — MacConkey agar: MacConkey agar is used for the gram negative bacilli and to show lactose fermentation

C — Robertson's cooked meat medium: Robertson's cooked meat medium is used for anaerobic organisms

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: Because the growth takes weeks, treatment is often started on the clinical picture and the staining report, and is reviewed when the culture is available

question: A nurse collects a wound swab at eight in the morning but it reaches the laboratory only at two in the afternoon. The result is likely to be:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. unreliable, because the organisms may have died or been overgrown by others

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Delay allows the delicate organisms to die and the hardy contaminants to multiply, so the report may mislead the treatment

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — more accurate than usual: Delay never improves the accuracy of a culture

C — reported as sterile in every case: A delay does not always give a sterile report, which makes it more dangerous as it may show a wrong organism

D — unaffected, as the swab keeps for a day: A swab is not a stable specimen and must reach the laboratory without delay

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The specimen is sent at once with the correct transport medium and a fully filled request form, since a poor specimen wastes the work of the laboratory and the money of the patient
option_1: unreliable, because the organisms may have died or been overgrown by others
option_4: unaffected, as the swab keeps for a day

question: Culture media and glassware in the laboratory are best sterilised by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. the autoclave

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Autoclaving with steam under pressure is the method of choice for media and glassware, as it kills the spores as well

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — boiling in water for five minutes: Boiling for a short time does not kill the spores

B — a disinfectant solution: A chemical disinfectant would remain in the medium and prevent growth

C — ultraviolet light: Ultraviolet light acts only on surfaces and does not penetrate the media

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: Media containing sugar are sterilised at a lower temperature or by filtration, since heat destroys the sugar

question: The staining method used to identify acid fast bacilli in a sputum smear is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. Ziehl-Neelsen staining

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Ziehl-Neelsen method uses carbol fuchsin with heat, and the bacilli retain the red colour even after being washed with acid and alcohol

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — Albert staining: Albert stain is used to show the metachromatic granules of the diphtheria bacilli

B — Leishman staining: Leishman stain is used for blood films and for cells

D — Gram staining: Gram staining divides bacteria into gram positive and gram negative groups

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate sterilisation from disinfection, and bacteria from viruses - they are common distractors.

💎 PNC Pearl: The smear is examined under the oil immersion lens, and at least a hundred fields are looked at before a negative report is given

question: An increase in the number of cells in a tissue is known as:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. hyperplasia

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In hyperplasia the number of cells rises, as in the enlarged prostate or in the breast during pregnancy

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — necrosis: Necrosis is the death of the tissue

C — hypertrophy: In hypertrophy the cells become larger but their number does not increase

D — atrophy: Atrophy is a shrinkage of the tissue

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Hyperplasia may be a normal response to a stimulus, as in the breast, or may precede a tumour, as in the lining of the uterus, so its cause is always looked into

question: The type of inflammation in which pus is formed is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. suppurative inflammation

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Pus forming organisms such as the staphylococci attract a large number of neutrophils, which die and form the thick creamy discharge that is called pus

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — chronic granulomatous inflammation: Granulomatous inflammation is chronic and forms a collection of the cells seen in tuberculosis

B — fibrinous inflammation: A fibrinous inflammation produces a tough mesh of fibrin on a surface such as the pericardium

D — serous inflammation: A serous inflammation produces a watery fluid, as in a blister

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Pus in a closed space must be drained, since antibiotics alone cannot reach an abscess that has no blood supply

question: A 45-year-old man with long standing diabetes has a deep painless ulcer on the sole of his foot with thick callus around it and reduced sensation in the foot. The most likely type of ulcer is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. neuropathic ulcer

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Loss of sensation from diabetic neuropathy allows repeated unnoticed pressure, which produces a painless deep ulcer over a pressure point with callus around it

🔍 Key Clues: 45-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — tuberculous ulcer: A tuberculous ulcer is irregular and is associated with a chronic systemic illness

B — venous ulcer: A venous ulcer is shallow, usually situated above the ankle and painful

D — arterial ulcer: An arterial ulcer is very painful, with a pale cold foot and weak pulses

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The pressure is taken off the ulcer completely with a special footwear device, since an ulcer that continues to bear weight will not heal however good the treatment

question: The reversible replacement of one type of mature cell by another type within a tissue is called:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. metaplasia

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In metaplasia the cells change from one mature type to another, as when the lining of the airway changes in a long term smoker, and the change reverses if the stimulus is removed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — anaplasia: Anaplasia is the loss of differentiation seen in malignant tumours

B — dysplasia: Dysplasia is disordered growth with variation in the size and the shape of the cells

C — neoplasia: Neoplasia means a new growth, that is a tumour

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: Metaplasia and dysplasia are warning signs, since the change that has already begun may progress to a cancer if the irritant continues

question: The type of necrosis seen in tuberculosis is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. caseous necrosis

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Tuberculosis produces a soft, cheese like, yellowish white material that is called caseous necrosis

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — fat necrosis: Fat necrosis is seen in the breast and in acute pancreatitis

B — coagulative necrosis: Coagulative necrosis is seen in the heart and the kidney after an infarction

D — liquefactive necrosis: Liquefactive necrosis occurs in the brain and in abscesses

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The caseous material may soften and spread through a bronchus, which is how a cavity forms and the disease spreads within the lung

question: A 55-year-old man has painless blood in the urine and the urine cytology is reported as suspicious of a malignant tumour. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. treat this as urgent, arrange a urological referral with the reports and explain the tests that are likely to be done

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Painless haematuria in an older man must be investigated without delay, since many bladder and kidney tumours first show themselves in this way

🔍 Key Clues: 55-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — tell him that nothing can be done: Telling a patient that nothing can be done before the diagnosis is known is both wrong and cruel

C — start him on an antibiotic and take no other action: An antibiotic may be needed for an infection but does not rule out a growth, so referral is still required

D — reassure him that blood in the urine is harmless and review him after a month: Reassurance and delay allow a tumour that could have been treated to spread

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse explains that the examination of the bladder is uncomfortable but short, and that early treatment gives the best chance of cure
option_1: treat this as urgent, arrange a urological referral with the reports and explain the tests that are likely to be done
option_2: tell him that nothing can be done
option_3: start him on an antibiotic and take no other action
option_4: reassure him that blood in the urine is harmless and review him after a month

question: Which of the following changes in a cell is irreversible?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. necrosis with loss of the nucleus and rupture of the cell membrane

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Once the nucleus has gone and the membrane has ruptured, the cell cannot recover and the change is irreversible

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — swelling of the cell with reversible changes in the organelles: Early cell swelling recovers fully when the cause is removed

C — metaplasia of the lining of the airway: Metaplasia reverses when the irritant is removed

D — mild fatty change in the liver: Mild fatty change in the liver is reversible if the cause such as alcohol is withdrawn

⚠️ Exam Trap: Distinguish acute from chronic, and reversible from irreversible, before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The treatment of an infarct is therefore aimed at saving the surviving tissue around the dead area and at removing the cause before more cells reach the irreversible stage
option_1: necrosis with loss of the nucleus and rupture of the cell membrane
option_2: swelling of the cell with reversible changes in the organelles
option_3: metaplasia of the lining of the airway

question: The pH of the body fluids is kept within narrow limits mainly by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. the buffers of the blood, the lungs and the kidneys

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Buffers act within seconds, the lungs adjust the carbon dioxide within minutes and the kidneys excrete the fixed acids over hours, and together they hold the pH steady

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the skin and the sweat: Sweat has only a minor effect

C — the liver alone: The liver metabolises many substances but is not the main regulator of the pH

D — the bone marrow: The marrow produces blood cells and does not control the pH

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The lungs and the kidneys are the two organs that respond most to a disturbance, so their function is assessed whenever the blood gases are abnormal
option_1: the buffers of the blood, the lungs and the kidneys

question: The main end product of protein metabolism that is excreted by the kidney is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. urea

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The ammonia formed from the amino groups is converted in the liver into urea, which is carried by the blood to the kidney and excreted

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — cholesterol: Cholesterol is a fat and is not a product of protein metabolism

C — uric acid only: Uric acid comes from the breakdown of the purines and forms only a small part of the total

D — glucose: Glucose is the end product of carbohydrate metabolism

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: A high blood urea with a normal creatinine suggests dehydration or bleeding into the gut rather than kidney failure

question: The blood test most useful in detecting damage to the liver cells is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. serum transaminase level

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The transaminases, particularly the alanine transaminase, leak out of the damaged liver cells and rise in the blood, which makes them sensitive indicators

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — creatine kinase level: Creatine kinase is raised in damage to the skeletal muscle and the heart

B — serum amylase level: Amylase is raised in acute pancreatitis and in disease of the salivary glands

C — blood urea level: The blood urea reflects kidney function and protein metabolism

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options and units - define the quantity before choosing.

💎 PNC Pearl: The level is read along with the bilirubin and the prothrombin time, since the transaminases show the damage while the other two show how well the liver is working

question: The correct position for the patient while a nasogastric tube is being passed is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. sitting up with the head slightly flexed forward

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The upright position with the neck slightly flexed closes the airway and opens the oesophagus, which allows the tube to pass into the stomach

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — standing upright: Standing is unsafe and unnecessary

B — lying flat with the head turned to the left: Lying flat makes the tube more likely to enter the airway

C — lying prone with the head turned to the side: Lying prone obstructs the procedure and endangers the airway

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is asked to swallow a sip of water as the tube is advanced, which helps it to pass downwards and reduces retching
option_2: lying flat with the head turned to the left
option_3: lying prone with the head turned to the side
option_4: sitting up with the head slightly flexed forward

question: The correct way to give eardrops to an adult is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. pull the pinna upwards and backwards, instil the drops and keep the position for a few minutes

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In an adult the ear canal runs slightly upwards, so pulling the pinna up and back straightens it and allows the drops to reach the drum, and the position is held so that the drug does not run out

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — instil the drops with the head turned to the same side: Lying on the same side lets the drops run straight out again

B — warm the bottle in hot water and instil the whole contents: Hot water may overheat the drops and burn the canal

D — pull the pinna downwards and forwards: The pinna is pulled down and back in an infant and not in an adult

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The tip of the dropper is never touched to the ear, since this contaminates the bottle for the next patient
option_1: instil the drops with the head turned to the same side
option_2: warm the bottle in hot water and instil the whole contents
option_3: pull the pinna upwards and backwards, instil the drops and keep the position for a few minutes

question: A patient with an indwelling urinary catheter has passed no urine for two hours and complains of fullness and discomfort in the lower abdomen. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. check the tubing for kinks, look for a distended bladder, reposition the patient and report if the urine still does not drain

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The commonest cause is a kink or a clot, and the tubing, the bladder and the position are checked before any other step

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — record the nil output and wait for the next shift: Waiting allows the bladder to overdistend and causes pain, infection and kidney damage

C — pull on the catheter to dislodge the block: Pulling on the catheter injures the urethra and does not relieve the block

D — give a diuretic as ordered without further assessment: A diuretic given when the outflow is blocked worsens the distension

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: If the bladder is distended and the catheter will not drain, it is the doctor who irrigates or changes the catheter, and the nurse records the finding and the action taken
option_1: record the nil output and wait for the next shift
option_2: check the tubing for kinks, look for a distended bladder, reposition the patient and report if the urine still does not drain
option_3: pull on the catheter to dislodge the block
option_4: give a diuretic as ordered without further assessment

question: A pressure relieving mattress is used for a bedridden patient in order to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. distribute the body weight over a larger area and reduce the pressure on the bony points

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The mattress moulds to the body and spreads the weight, which lowers the pressure at the heels, the sacrum and the hips

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — keep the patient warm: Warmth is not the aim, although some mattresses do retain heat

C — replace the need for position changes: Turning the patient at regular intervals is still essential, since no mattress removes the need for it

D — prevent the patient from turning in bed: Immobility is not the purpose and may in fact be harmful

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: Even on such a mattress, the skin is inspected at every turn and the heels are lifted clear, as these are the commonest sites for a sore to begin
option_2: distribute the body weight over a larger area and reduce the pressure on the bony points
option_4: prevent the patient from turning in bed

question: The correct technique of giving a subcutaneous injection is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. pinch up the skin, insert the needle at 45 to 90 degrees, inject slowly and withdraw without massaging the site

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Pinching lifts the fat away from the muscle, the needle is inserted at an angle suited to the thickness of the fat, and the site is not massaged because massage alters the rate of absorption

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — use a long needle to reach the muscle below the fat: A long needle would deliver the drug into the muscle, which is the intramuscular and not the subcutaneous route

C — inject into the deltoid muscle: The deltoid is used for the intramuscular route

D — insert the needle at 15 degrees and massage the site firmly afterwards: A fifteen degree angle would deposit the drug too close to the surface, and massage is avoided

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The sites are rotated, since repeated injections into the same spot produce hard lumps and poor absorption
option_1: use a long needle to reach the muscle below the fat
option_2: pinch up the skin, insert the needle at 45 to 90 degrees, inject slowly and withdraw without massaging the site
option_4: insert the needle at 15 degrees and massage the site firmly afterwards

question: The normal systolic blood pressure of a healthy young adult is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 120 millimetres of mercury

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The usual systolic pressure of a healthy young adult is about one hundred and twenty millimetres of mercury, with the diastolic at about eighty

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — 90 millimetres of mercury: Ninety is the lower end of the normal systolic range and is low for a young adult

C — 180 millimetres of mercury: One hundred and eighty is high and indicates severe hypertension

D — 60 millimetres of mercury: Sixty is a low diastolic value

⚠️ Exam Trap: In FIRST-action questions, identify the life-threatening problem and stabilise or assess before anything else.

💎 PNC Pearl: The blood pressure is recorded with the patient at rest, the arm supported at heart level and a cuff of the correct size, since all three affect the reading

question: The normal capillary refill time at the nail bed of a healthy adult is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. less than three seconds

🧠 Clinical Rationale: After the nail bed is pressed and released the colour returns within about three seconds, which shows that the peripheral circulation is adequate

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — five to six seconds: A delay of five to six seconds indicates poor perfusion

B — less than one second: A less than one second refill is not usual and may be seen with a fever

D — eight to ten seconds: A delay of eight to ten seconds indicates severe circulatory failure and shock

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The test is done on a warm finger, since cold makes the refill slow even in a well patient, and the finding is read along with the pulse and the blood pressure

question: A patient who had an abdominal operation three days ago has a distended abdomen, has not passed flatus and the bowel sounds are absent. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. keep the patient nil by mouth, report the finding, pass a prescribed nasogastric tube for decompression and encourage gentle movement once allowed

🧠 Clinical Rationale: This is paralytic ileus, in which the bowel has stopped moving after operation, and it is treated by resting the gut, decompressing it and correcting the cause

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give a large enema immediately: An enema does not help an ileus and may cause harm

C — give a heavy meal to stimulate the bowel: Food given while the bowel is not moving accumulates and causes vomiting

D — give a strong purgative at once: A purgative can cause a dangerous distension in a bowel that is not moving

⚠️ Exam Trap: Read the stem twice - one word such as MOST or EXCEPT can reverse the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The return of bowel sounds and the passing of flatus are the signs that feeding can begin, and they are recorded at every shift
option_2: keep the patient nil by mouth, report the finding, pass a prescribed nasogastric tube for decompression and encourage gentle movement once allowed
option_3: give a heavy meal to stimulate the bowel

question: Before a hot water bottle is applied to a patient the nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. fill it two thirds with hot water, expel the air, check that it does not leak and wrap it in a cloth

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A partly filled bottle does not burst, the air is expelled so that the heat is even, and the cloth prevents a burn

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — apply it directly on the bare skin: Direct contact with the skin causes burns, particularly in an unconscious or elderly patient

C — leave it in place for several hours without checking the skin: Prolonged application without checking the skin leads to a burn before the patient can feel or report it

D — fill it completely with boiling water: Filling with boiling water makes the bottle too hot and may burst it

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The skin is inspected every few minutes, and heat is never applied over an area of numbness, poor circulation or a recent injury
option_1: fill it two thirds with hot water, expel the air, check that it does not leak and wrap it in a cloth
option_2: apply it directly on the bare skin
option_3: leave it in place for several hours without checking the skin

question: Deep breathing and coughing exercises are taught after an operation in order to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. expand the lungs, remove the secretions and prevent chest infection and collapse of the lung

🧠 Clinical Rationale: After an operation the lungs do not expand fully because of the pain and the anaesthetic, and the retained secretions cause infection or collapse of part of the lung

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — help the bowel to move: Movement of the bowel is encouraged by early walking, fluids and a suitable diet

C — reduce the pain of the wound: The exercises may in fact cause some discomfort, which is why the wound is supported

D — prevent bed sores: Bed sores are prevented by turning and by skin care

⚠️ Exam Trap: Do not pick an option only because it is familiar - the option that fits the whole stem is the answer.

💎 PNC Pearl: The wound is supported with both hands or a pillow during the cough, which allows the patient to cough effectively despite the pain
option_2: expand the lungs, remove the secretions and prevent chest infection and collapse of the lung

question: The best sputum specimen for examination is collected:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. early in the morning, from the depth of the chest, after rinsing the mouth

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The secretions collect in the chest overnight, so an early morning specimen coughed from deep in the chest gives the best chance of finding the organism, and rinsing reduces the mouth organisms

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — at any time with a mouth swab: A mouth swab does not collect the lung secretions at all

B — from the saliva in the mouth: Saliva contains mouth organisms and not the organisms from the lung

D — after a meal: A specimen after a meal contains more food and mouth contents

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The patient is taught to take three deep breaths and then cough out the sputum and not to spit saliva, since a poor specimen may give a false negative report
option_1: at any time with a mouth swab
option_3: early in the morning, from the depth of the chest, after rinsing the mouth

question: The correct order of the steps of a blood transfusion is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. check the order and the unit against the identity of the patient, take the baseline vital signs, start the transfusion slowly, observe closely for the first fifteen minutes and then set the prescribed rate

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The identity of the patient and the details of the unit are checked at the bedside by two persons, and the slow start with close observation detects a reaction while only a small quantity has been given

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — warm the blood in hot water before starting: Blood is warmed only by a special warmer, as hot water damages the cells

B — start the transfusion rapidly and check the details afterwards: Starting rapidly before the checks may mean that the wrong unit reaches the wrong patient

C — give the unit without taking the vital signs: The baseline vital signs are needed for comparison when a reaction is suspected

⚠️ Exam Trap: In procedure questions choose the step that protects the patient first - safety before comfort and speed.

💎 PNC Pearl: The unit is not left hanging for more than four hours, since bacterial growth becomes a real risk after that time
option_1: warm the blood in hot water before starting
option_2: start the transfusion rapidly and check the details afterwards
option_3: give the unit without taking the vital signs
option_4: check the order and the unit against the identity of the patient, take the baseline vital signs, start the transfusion slowly, observe closely for the first fifteen minutes and then set the prescribed rate

question: The correct action during a generalised convulsion in an adult patient is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. protect the patient from injury, loosen the clothing at the neck, turn the head to the side and never restrain the limbs or put anything in the mouth

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The aim is to protect the patient from a fall and from injury while allowing the fit to complete its own course, and turning the head prevents aspiration

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give a drink of water as soon as the fit begins: Fluid given during a fit will be inhaled into the lungs

B — hold the limbs down firmly: Restraining the limbs causes fractures and injuries

D — force a spoon between the teeth: A spoon may break the teeth, block the airway or be bitten through

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: The time of the fit, the parts of the body involved, the duration and the state after the fit are recorded, since these details decide the choice and the dose of the drug
option_1: give a drink of water as soon as the fit begins
option_3: protect the patient from injury, loosen the clothing at the neck, turn the head to the side and never restrain the limbs or put anything in the mouth

question: The normal fetal heart rate is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 120 to 160 beats per minute

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A rate between one hundred and twenty and one hundred and sixty beats a minute is normal in a healthy fetus

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 80 to 100 beats per minute: A rate of eighty to a hundred is bradycardia and suggests fetal distress

B — 60 to 80 beats per minute: A rate of sixty to eighty is incompatible with fetal wellbeing

C — 170 to 200 beats per minute: A rate above one hundred and seventy is tachycardia and needs investigation

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The rate is listened to for a full minute, between contractions, in both the first and the second stages of labour

question: The onset of the second stage of labour is marked by:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. full dilatation of the cervix with the mother having an urge to bear down

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The second stage begins when the cervix is fully dilated and ends with the birth of the baby, and the mother feels a strong urge to push

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — regular contractions every ten minutes: Contractions every ten minutes are seen in the early first stage

B — the passing of the mucus plug: The mucus plug is passed before labour begins or in the early first stage

D — the rupture of the membranes: The membranes may rupture in any stage of labour

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The fetal heart rate is checked every five minutes or after every contraction in the second stage, since the pressure on the head during this period can cause distress
option_3: full dilatation of the cervix with the mother having an urge to bear down

question: The medicine put into the eyes of every newborn shortly after birth is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. an antibacterial eye ointment, to prevent infection of the eyes from the birth canal

🧠 Clinical Rationale: An antibacterial ointment such as tetracycline or erythromycin is applied to both eyes to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum, which is acquired from the mother's genital tract

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — normal saline only: Normal saline cleans but does not prevent infection

C — a steroid eye ointment: A steroid has no role at birth and may worsen an infection

D — atropine drops: Atropine dilates the pupil and is used in eye examination and in some treatments

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The cord stump is also kept clean and dry, and the mother is taught to wash her hands before handling the eyes and the cord of the baby
option_1: an antibacterial eye ointment, to prevent infection of the eyes from the birth canal

question: The correct method of collecting a cervical smear is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. take the smear from the transformation zone with a spatula or brush, spread it evenly on the slide and fix it at once

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Almost all cancers of the cervix begin at the transformation zone, and the cells must be spread and fixed quickly so that they do not dry and become unreadable

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — collect the sample from the external surface of the cervix only: A smear from the outer surface alone misses a lesion within the canal

C — collect the sample after douching the vagina: Douching washes away the cells and alters the picture

D — take the sample during the period of bleeding: The smear is best taken in the middle of the cycle and not during the period, when the blood obscures the cells

⚠️ Exam Trap: In obstetric questions ask who is at immediate risk, mother or fetus - that decides the first action.

💎 PNC Pearl: The woman is told that a slightly blood stained discharge for a day afterwards is normal, so that she is not alarmed
option_1: take the smear from the transformation zone with a spatula or brush, spread it evenly on the slide and fix it at once
option_2: collect the sample from the external surface of the cervix only
option_3: collect the sample after douching the vagina
option_4: take the sample during the period of bleeding

question: The minimum number of antenatal visits recommended for a woman with a normal pregnancy is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. at least four

🧠 Clinical Rationale: At least four visits are recommended, one in each trimester and one in the last month, so that the progress of the pregnancy and the danger signs are reviewed

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — ten: Ten visits are not needed for a normal pregnancy

B — only when there is a problem: Visits only when there is a problem miss the chance to prevent complications

D — one: A single visit cannot cover the changes that occur through the pregnancy

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: At every visit the weight, the blood pressure, the haemoglobin and the fetal heart are recorded, along with the advice given

question: The correct way of preparing oral rehydration solution at home is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. dissolve one packet in one litre of clean water and use it within twenty four hours

🧠 Clinical Rationale: One packet to one litre of clean water gives the correct concentration, and the solution is discarded after twenty four hours because it becomes contaminated

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — keep the prepared solution for a week: A week old solution is heavily contaminated and its salts have separated

B — dissolve one packet in a cup of water: Using a cup makes the solution too strong, which worsens the diarrhoea

C — add sugar and salt to the solution to make it stronger: Adding sugar and salt upsets the balance and can cause harm

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The mother is asked to prepare the solution in front of the nurse at least once, since a mixture made by guesswork often fails and the child is brought back dehydrated
option_1: keep the prepared solution for a week
option_2: dissolve one packet in a cup of water
option_3: add sugar and salt to the solution to make it stronger
option_4: dissolve one packet in one litre of clean water and use it within twenty four hours

question: The vaccines given to a newborn at birth under the national immunisation schedule are:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. BCG, the birth dose of oral polio vaccine and the birth dose of hepatitis B

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The three birth doses protect the baby at the time when the risk of tuberculosis and hepatitis B is highest

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — measles and vitamin A: Measles is given at nine months and vitamin A with it

B — DPT and oral polio vaccine: DPT is started at six weeks

C — typhoid and chickenpox vaccines: Neither typhoid nor chickenpox vaccine forms part of the routine schedule

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: The dates of each dose are written on the mother's card and explained, since a child who misses a dose can still be brought up to date at the next visit
option_4: BCG, the birth dose of oral polio vaccine and the birth dose of hepatitis B

question: The single most effective measure to reduce diarrhoeal disease in a village is to provide:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. safe drinking water along with proper disposal of excreta and hand washing with soap

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Diarrhoea is spread by the faecal oral route, so breaking that route at the level of the water, the excreta and the hands prevents the disease rather than treating it

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — free medicines at the health centre: Free medicines treat the illness after it has occurred

B — oral rehydration packets in every house: Oral rehydration packets save lives after the diarrhoea has begun but do not prevent it

D — vitamin A to all children: Vitamin A reduces the severity of some infections but is not the main preventive measure here

⚠️ Exam Trap: In community health questions ask whether the action is at family, community or facility level.

💎 PNC Pearl: Hand washing with soap after defecation and before feeding is the cheapest single measure, and the nurse demonstrates it in the homes
option_3: safe drinking water along with proper disposal of excreta and hand washing with soap

question: The normal head circumference of a newborn baby is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 33 to 35 centimetres

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The head circumference at birth is about thirty three to thirty five centimetres and exceeds the chest circumference by about two centimetres

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 50 centimetres: Fifty centimetres is the average circumference of an adult head

B — 25 centimetres: Twenty five centimetres is far too small and indicates severe microcephaly

D — 45 centimetres: Forty five centimetres is larger than normal at birth

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: A head that grows too fast suggests hydrocephalus, and one that grows too slowly suggests a failure of brain growth, so the measurement is plotted on the chart at every visit

question: The birth weight of a healthy infant is usually doubled by the age of:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. five months

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A healthy infant doubles the birth weight by about five months and triples it by the first birthday

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — one month: One month is far too early for the weight to double

B — one year: By one year the weight is about three times the birth weight

D — two years: At two years the weight is about four times the birth weight

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The weight is plotted on the growth chart each month, since the trend is a better guide to the health of the child than a single reading

question: A newborn baby is noticed to be jaundiced within the first twenty four hours of birth. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. treat it as abnormal, report at once, check the bilirubin and the blood groups of the mother and the baby and prepare for treatment as ordered

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Jaundice within the first day is always pathological and may be due to a blood group incompatibility or an infection, so it is investigated and treated without delay

🔍 Key Clues: newborn

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — give the baby extra water between feeds and wait: Extra water does not treat the cause and delays the treatment

C — reassure the mother that all babies become yellow on the third day: Physiological jaundice appears after the first day and not within twenty four hours

D — keep the baby in the sun and review after a week: Sunlight is not a treatment for this and a week's delay may allow damage to the brain

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The bilirubin level is checked at intervals, since a rapidly rising value can lead to kernicterus, and the baby is fed frequently to help the excretion of the pigment
option_1: treat it as abnormal, report at once, check the bilirubin and the blood groups of the mother and the baby and prepare for treatment as ordered
option_2: give the baby extra water between feeds and wait
option_3: reassure the mother that all babies become yellow on the third day
option_4: keep the baby in the sun and review after a week

question: The best way to feed a newborn who has a cleft lip is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. hold the baby upright, use a soft bottle with a large hole or a spoon and feed slowly, and use expressed breast milk

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The upright position prevents the milk from entering the nose, and a large soft teat or a spoon feeds the baby with the least effort, with breast milk still given

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — feed only with a spoon: A spoon alone is slow and tiring for both the baby and the mother

C — stop breastfeeding altogether: Breast milk is the best food and is continued through expression and direct breast feeding where possible

D — lay the baby flat and feed with a fast flowing bottle: Lying flat causes choking and regurgitation through the nose

⚠️ Exam Trap: In paediatric questions look at the age first - the normal values and the expected action change with age.

💎 PNC Pearl: The baby is also checked for a cleft palate, since a defect of the palate makes feeding far more difficult and may need a special obturator
option_2: hold the baby upright, use a soft bottle with a large hole or a spoon and feed slowly, and use expressed breast milk
option_4: lay the baby flat and feed with a fast flowing bottle

question: The normal number of white blood cells per cubic millimetre of blood is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. 4000 to 11,000

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Between about four thousand and eleven thousand white cells per cubic millimetre is the normal range in an adult

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 500,000 to 1,000,000: This range belongs to the platelets

B — 100 to 500: This range is far below the normal white cell count

C — 40,000 to 50,000: This range suggests leukaemia

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: A rise in the white cell count usually indicates a bacterial infection, and a fall is seen in some viral infections and after certain drugs

question: Bile is produced by the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. liver

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The liver produces bile continuously, and it is stored and concentrated in the gall bladder

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — pancreas: The pancreas secretes the pancreatic enzymes and bicarbonate

B — gall bladder: The gall bladder stores and concentrates bile but does not produce it

D — stomach: The stomach secretes acid and enzymes that digest protein

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: Bile salts are needed for the digestion and the absorption of fat, which is why a patient with a blocked bile duct passes pale, bulky stools

question: The part of a neuron that conducts impulses away from the cell body is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. axon

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The axon is the single long process that carries the impulse away from the cell body to the next cell

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — myelin sheath: The myelin sheath is the insulating covering that speeds the conduction along the axon

B — synapse: A synapse is the junction between two neurons and not a part of the neuron

D — dendrite: The dendrites receive impulses and carry them towards the cell body

⚠️ Exam Trap: Know the definition AND the unit - exams love near-sounding concepts.

💎 PNC Pearl: Demyelination slows the conduction of the impulses and produces weakness, numbness and loss of coordination

question: The main purpose of group therapy is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. help the members to learn from one another and from their own interaction within a supervised group

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The interaction among the members itself becomes the treatment, as each member sees his own difficulties reflected in others and receives support and feedback

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give each member individual attention from the therapist: Individual attention is limited in a group and is not the aim

B — replace drug treatment: Group therapy works along with medication and does not replace it

C — keep the patients busy during the day: An activity programme keeps patients occupied; group therapy has a defined therapeutic purpose

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse sets clear rules about confidentiality and attendance, since the group is useful only when the members feel safe enough to speak
option_1: give each member individual attention from the therapist
option_3: keep the patients busy during the day

question: A 30-year-old woman who has just delivered a stillborn baby refuses to meet anyone and cries continuously. The nurse should:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. stay with her, allow her to grieve and express her feelings, answer her questions honestly and assess her for depression

🧠 Clinical Rationale: Grief must be allowed to run its course, and a calm presence with honest answers helps the mother and lets the nurse detect a depression that needs treatment

🔍 Key Clues: 30-year-old

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — give her a sedative and avoid the subject of the baby: Sedation and silence deny the loss and delay the natural grieving

C — tell her that she is young and can have another baby: Such words dismiss the loss and increase her sense of isolation

D — shift her at once to a ward where there are other mothers: Placing her among mothers with babies adds to her distress and is done only when she is ready

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: The family is also supported, and the mother is told that crying, sleeplessness and a sense of emptiness are normal at first but that a continued inability to function needs help
option_1: give her a sedative and avoid the subject of the baby

option_3: tell her that she is young and can have another baby

question: The daily protein requirement of a healthy adult is about:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. 1 gram per kilogram of body weight

🧠 Clinical Rationale: About one gram of protein for each kilogram of body weight meets the needs of a healthy adult, and the requirement rises in pregnancy, growth and recovery from illness

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 0.1 gram per kilogram of body weight: A tenth of a gram per kilogram leads to protein deficiency

C — 10 grams per kilogram of body weight: Ten grams per kilogram is neither needed nor possible

D — 5 grams per kilogram of body weight: Five grams per kilogram is far above the requirement and burdens the kidney

⚠️ Exam Trap: Separate the deficiency disease from its dietary source - exams mix the two.

💎 PNC Pearl: The quality matters as well as the quantity, so a mixture of cereals and pulses is advised, as this gives a better range of amino acids than either alone
option_1: 0.1 gram per kilogram of body weight
option_2: 1 gram per kilogram of body weight
option_3: 10 grams per kilogram of body weight
option_4: 5 grams per kilogram of body weight

question: The main purpose of an indenting system in a ward is to:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. ensure the timely supply of the drugs and materials needed for patient care in the right quantity

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The indent is prepared from the actual consumption and the stock on hand, which keeps the supply in step with the needs of the ward

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — keep the store room full at all times: Overstocking leads to expiry and wastage

C — reduce the number of nurses: The indent has no relation to the number of staff

D — check the honesty of the staff: The indent is a supply document and not a check on honesty

⚠️ Exam Trap: Remember that delegation transfers the task but never the accountability.

💎 PNC Pearl: Emergency drugs, oxygen and sterile supplies are checked at every shift, since a shortage discovered at the time of need is already too late
option_1: keep the store room full at all times
option_2: ensure the timely supply of the drugs and materials needed for patient care in the right quantity

question: The abstract of a research report is:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a brief summary of the whole study placed at the beginning of the report

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The abstract condenses the problem, the method, the main findings and the conclusion into a short paragraph so that a reader can judge whether the full paper is of interest

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the list of references: References are listed at the end

C — the raw data of the study: Raw data are kept as appendices or in a separate file

D — the letter of permission from the ethics committee: The permission letter is part of the study documents and not of the report

⚠️ Exam Trap: In research questions define the term precisely - reliability, validity and sampling are often interchanged.

💎 PNC Pearl: An abstract must not make claims that the results do not support, which is why it is written last of all
option_1: a brief summary of the whole study placed at the beginning of the report
option_4: the letter of permission from the ethics committee

question: According to Freud, the part of the personality that works on the reality principle and mediates between the other two parts is the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. ego

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The ego deals with reality, balancing the demands of the id with the standards of the superego and the demands of the outside world

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — id: The id works on the pleasure principle and seeks immediate satisfaction

C — conscience: The conscience is one part of the superego and not a separate structure

D — superego: The superego represents the internalised moral standards of the person

⚠️ Exam Trap: In mental health questions, choose the response that is non-judgemental and preserves safety first.

💎 PNC Pearl: A person under great stress may show behaviour that is dominated by the id, which is why the nurse sets clear and consistent limits for a disturbed patient

question: Which of the following is an example of a secondary group in society?
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. a trade union

🧠 Clinical Rationale: A secondary group is large, formally organised and based on a specific purpose rather than on personal ties, and a trade union is an example

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — the family: The family is the primary group

C — a play group of children: A play group of children has face to face personal ties and is a primary group

D — a group of close friends: Close friends form a primary group

⚠️ Exam Trap: Be careful with absolute words such as ALWAYS and NEVER unless the fact is truly absolute.

💎 PNC Pearl: Health behaviour is influenced by both, as the family shapes daily habits while a workplace union or a self help group can support the use of services

question: A person who is a carrier of a genetic disorder:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. carries one copy of the abnormal gene without having the disease and can pass it on to the children

🧠 Clinical Rationale: In a recessive disorder the carrier has one normal and one abnormal allele, remains healthy but may transmit the abnormal gene

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — can never have an affected child: Two carriers have a one in four chance of having an affected child

C — is completely free of the abnormal gene: The abnormal gene is certainly present

D — has the disease in a mild form: The carrier state produces no disease at all

⚠️ Exam Trap: For genetic questions work out the pattern of inheritance before the probability.

💎 PNC Pearl: Carrier testing and genetic counselling are offered to the relatives of an affected person, since most carriers are unaware of their status until an affected child is born
option_1: carries one copy of the abnormal gene without having the disease and can pass it on to the children

option_4: has the disease in a mild form

question: World Pharmacists Day is observed every year on:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. 25 September

❌ Why Not Other Options?

question: National Science Day in India is observed every year on:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. 28 February

🧠 Clinical Rationale: National Science Day marks the announcement of the Raman effect on the twenty eighth of February and is used to promote scientific temper

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — 26 January: The twenty sixth of January is Republic Day

B — 15 August: The fifteenth of August is Independence Day

D — 5 June: The fifth of June is World Environment Day

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The day is used in schools and colleges to explain the science behind health practices such as immunisation and hand washing

question: The Drug Controller General of India is responsible for:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. approving new drugs and regulating their manufacture, import and sale

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The office is the national authority for the approval of drugs, clinical trials and the standards of manufacture, import and sale

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — running the government hospitals: Hospitals are administered by the health departments of the states

C — fixing the prices of all medicines: Prices of essential medicines are controlled by a separate pricing authority

D — conducting the census: The census is conducted by the Registrar General of India

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: A drug that has not been approved cannot legally be supplied, which is why the nurse checks the label and the batch details of any medicine received in the ward
option_1: approving new drugs and regulating their manufacture, import and sale

question: The standards of quality for drugs in India are laid down by the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission publishes the official standards that every drug manufactured or imported in India must meet

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — Indian Council of Agricultural Research: The agricultural research council deals with agriculture and animal science

C — National Sample Survey Office: The sample survey office conducts socio economic surveys

D — Food Corporation of India: The Food Corporation deals with the storage and distribution of food grains

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The pharmacopoeia gives the tests for identity, purity and strength, and a drug that fails these tests is not fit for use even if the label looks correct

question: The Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan is a campaign against:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: c. tobacco and substance abuse

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The campaign aims at preventing and reducing the use of drugs, alcohol and tobacco, and at rehabilitating those who are dependent on them

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — child labour: Child labour is dealt with by the labour laws and child protection services

B — open defecation: Open defecation is addressed by the sanitation mission

D — air pollution: Air pollution is addressed by environmental regulations

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

💎 PNC Pearl: The nurse screens for substance use during routine visits, since an early brief intervention at the clinic is more effective than treatment after dependence has set in

question: The National Blood Transfusion Council in India is concerned with:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: b. the collection, testing, storage and safe supply of blood and blood products

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The council oversees the blood banks and lays down the standards for testing, storage and the rational use of blood and its components

❌ Why Not Other Options?

A — the regulation of pharmacies: Pharmacies are regulated under the drugs and cosmetics rules

C — the manufacture of vaccines: Vaccine production is the work of the vaccine institutes

D — the training of nurses: The training of nurses is regulated by the nursing councils

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

option_2: the collection, testing, storage and safe supply of blood and blood products

question: The Pharmacovigilance Programme of India is coordinated at the national level by the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: a. Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission at Ghaziabad

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission acts as the national coordination centre that collects and analyses reports of adverse drug reactions from the whole country

❌ Why Not Other Options?

B — National Institute of Nutrition at Hyderabad: The nutrition institute works on nutrition research

C — Central Drug Research Institute at Lucknow: The drug research institute carries out research on drugs and does not coordinate this programme

⚠️ Exam Trap: Beware near-sounding options (Delhi vs New Delhi, Godavari vs Ganga).

option_4: All India Institute of Medical Sciences at Delhi

question: The manufacture, sale and distribution of drugs in India are regulated by the:
solution:
✅ Correct Answer: d. Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940

🧠 Clinical Rationale: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act and the rules made under it control the import, manufacture, distribution and sale of drugs and cosmetics in the country
